name: Ernest Scarfe
bio: A valet's son and sometime valet, 'a young man of about twenty' by Wilde's sworn estimate, who went out to the Australian gold-diggings in 1893 — meeting Lord Douglas of Hawick, Bosie's elder brother, on the voyage — and returned to a clerkship in St Paul's Churchyard. He knew Taylor from the Knightsbridge Skating Rink; Taylor introduced him to Wilde at 10 St James's Place, where the waiter counted five or six visits, and he dined alone with Wilde and received the customary £4 cigarette case, last dining with him at the Avondale Hotel in February 1895. Queensberry's plea alleged solicitation and gross indecency at St James's Place (Oct 1893-Apr 1894); Scarfe was never called and no charge was ever laid; a begging letter from 'Ernesto' that Wilde mentions to Douglas in mid-1894 is tentatively identified with him by the Letters editors.
bio_sources: Wilde's libel-trial cross-examination, Hyde, Trials (1948), pp. 148-149, 152 (djvu OCR)
Taylor's testimony, Hyde, Trials (1948), p. 286 (IIIF page image 2026-08-03)
Thomas Price's testimony, Hyde, Trials (1948), pp. 205-206 (djvu OCR)
Hyde, Trials (1948), Introduction p. 47 n (the Hawick voyage acquaintance, 1893; djvu OCR)
Queensberry's plea, Hyde, Trials (1948), p. 343 (IIIF page image 2026-08-03)

bio_note: Dates: not found; recorded as unrecovered from the sources consulted. The Complete Letters editors do not identify him beyond a hesitant footnote: the recipient of an 1894 letter is glossed 'Possibly Ernest Scarfe, a valet (see Trials, pp.148-9)' - located in the OCR mirror at PDF 650 (printed folio around 598, not confirmed in the source) - and the General Index entry is the cross-reference 'Ernesto see Scarfe, Ernest'. Searched: the Complete Letters (2000) OCR mirror plus the General Index; McKenna, The Secret Life of Oscar Wilde (2008), PDF; Murray, Bosie (2020), PDF; Frankel, The Unrepentant Years (2017), PDF; Hyde, The Trials of Oscar Wilde, in the Internet Archive copy (item in.ernet.dli.2015.499238, OCR text downloaded and searched, key pages then read as page images); and the open web. No birth or death date is recorded in any source consulted.
